title: tenant-conntrack-hot-swap-isolation-fix
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
A production customer on Dedicated experienced intermittent cross-tenant hostname resolution and transient TCP connections to the wrong tenant after a scheduled GPU pool hot-swap. Symptoms included brief success responses to DNS queries followed by responses containing private hostnames from a different tenant, and connection resets for in-flight requests during the migration window.

Incident timeline (abridged):
- 2026-02-24 03:12 UTC: Scheduled GPU host drain for capacity rebalance. Autoscaler initiated live migration and SNAT pool handoff.
- 2026-02-24 03:15 UTC: First customer report — app observed stray DNS answers for internal hostnames.
- 2026-02-24 03:22 UTC: Multiple tenants reported intermittent 5xx for short (10-30s) windows.
- 2026-02-24 04:00 UTC: Escalation to on-call network and runtime teams. Temporary mitigation applied: pause migrations and pin affected tenant to previous host.

Reproduction notes:
- Can be reproduced in staging by performing a host drain while simultaneously triggering a resolver failover and high-connection churn on the affected tenant.
- Packet captures show DNS responses with correct source IP but payloads containing cached PTR/A records from another tenant. Conntrack entries show reflected NAT mappings shortly after the host swap.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed):
- During hot-swap, the conntrack namespace used for tenant SNATs is not fully isolated for a 10-30s window when an internal control-plane reconciliation retries route rebinds.
- A timing window exists where new ephemeral SNAT mappings are created in the global conntrack table before the endpoint-level namespace policy is reapplied. If the resolver process is moved or a local resolver cache is drained concurrently, responses can be associated with the wrong tenant socket via conntrack reflection.
- Secondary contributor: overlay encapsulation (VXLAN/EVPN) offload + host-side kernel conntrack garbage collection heuristics cause delayed teardown of stale entries, widening the exposure window.

Immediate mitigation implemented:
- Reverted host drain for impacted capacity pools and pinned active connections to the source host while a hotfix was prepared.
- Deployed a control-plane guard that delays route rebinds until conntrack namespace switch-confirm ACKs are observed (rolled to 20% of hosts in the pool).

Proposed long-term fix (plan):
1) Patch the runtime agent to perform an atomic conntrack namespace swap during VIP handoffs. The agent will:
   - Create per-tenant ephemeral conntrack namespaces at attach time.
   - Use a double-buffering technique to commit new namespace and atomically flip iptables/nft rules to target the new namespace.
2) Introduce a preflight probe before removing old SNAT pools: send conformance probes for a tenant's resolver and primary ports to confirm no active mappings remain.
3) Update host kernel tuning: reduce nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established for the maintenance window to ensure faster teardown during migration, gated behind the runtime agent flag.
4) Add e2e integration tests in our chaos suite that simulate hot-swap + resolver failover under load.

Rollout strategy:
- Patch branch: runtime-agent#PR-8672 (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8672)
- Canary: deploy to 10% of Dedicated GPU hosts in non-critical region for 48 hours with synthetic traffic and observability probes enabled.
- Gradual increase to 100% after 72h if no regressions.
- Post-deploy: monitor resolver error rate, cross-tenant DNS hitrate, conntrack namespace counts, and per-tenant connection anomalies.

QA and test plan:
- Add unit tests for namespace flip logic and mock kernel behavior.
- Add integration test in chaos lab that triggers host drain + resolver restart with high churn; assert zero cross-tenant DNS payloads and stable conntrack counts.
- Manual verification with affected customer test account prior to broad rollout.

Monitoring & alerting changes:
- New alert: conntrack-namespace-swap-failures (threshold: >5 fails in 1m for a host).
- Dashboard panels: per-host conntrack namespace counts, per-tenant SNAT mappings, DNS payload origin histogram.

Customer comms:
- Initial notice sent to customer SREs on 2026-02-24 with mitigation steps and ETA for fix.
- Follow-up scheduled after stabilized canary and before full rollout.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we require a full kernel backport for older Dedicated host images, or can runtime-agent feature gate suffice? (PO decision required)
- Should we include aggressive conntrack GC changes outside maintenance windows or only during host swap operations?

Artifacts and links:
- Incident board (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-02-24+Tenant+Conntrack+Reflection
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8672
- Troubleshooting packet captures: GCS: gs://redwood-incident-captures/2026-02-24/conntrack-reflection.pcap
- Customer support thread: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/incident-2026-02-24-thread

Next steps (short-term):
- Complete PR review and land runtime-agent patch (owner: Miguel Torres) — target 2026-03-11.
- Run chaos-suite integration test and validate with synthetic tenant traffic — target 2026-03-12.
- Begin canary rollout 2026-03-13 and monitor for 72h.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Patch merged and rolled to 100% of Dedicated hosts.
- No further cross-tenant DNS or connection leakage incidents observed for 14 days post-rollout.
- Postmortem published with mitigation timeline and lessons learned.
